newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: W&H shareholders seen reluctant sellers.
newsitem.headline: W&H shareholders seen reluctant sellers.

text.p: New Zealand analysts said on Monday that shareholders in publisher Wilson and Horton Ltd may seek a higher price than the NZ$10.50/share takeover offer by Ireland's Independent Newspapers Plc.
"Perhaps it may be seen as just a little bit opportunistic," said ANZ Securities Managing Director Tim Preston.
"There may be people in the market who feel that the underlying business and the franchise...may well be worth a bit more."
Wilson and Horton closed on Monday at $9.70.

Brokers said Independent had a sound rationale for seeking to move to 100 percent ownership, but the timing had caught the market by surprise. Independent currently has an effective 22.6 percent stake through its 50 percent interest in three companies which hold 45.15 percent of Wilson and Horton.
Wilson and Horton issued a notice advising shareholders not to sell for the time being. John Rowley of brokers SBC Warburg said an independent appraisal report on the bid would be "intriguing".
